sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Peoria County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Peoria County splits the tax job among four courthouse offices. One official acts as both Treasurer and County Collector, so the bill and the payment counter are in the same place. Valuation sits with the Supervisor of Assessments, disputes go to the Board of Review, and the County Clerk turns levies into rates and later receives money for any year that was sold. Your first call about value belongs with the township assessor.

The county lies along the Illinois River. Organized in 1825 from part of Fulton County, it measures 631 square miles and names the city of Peoria as its seat. Peoria and West Peoria are treated as independent of the surrounding townships, so a house in either place deals with a city township office while a rural parcel deals with its own township.

  • Treasurer: mails and collects the bills from 324 Main Street, Room G15.
  • Supervisor of Assessments: publishes assessment changes and handles exemption questions at 309-672-6910.
  • Board of Review: three people named by the County Board, working from Room 301.
  • County Clerk: extends the tax rate and receives payment of sold taxes at Room 101.

sections.h2: What do Peoria County's numbers say about homes and owners?
sections.html:
For July 2025 QuickFacts estimates 178,553 residents, which is 1.9% below the 2020 base. The county has 84,884 housing units. Households number 77,755, and 67.0% of them own their home, with a 2020-2024 median value of $158,500.

Median rent is $993 and median household income is $65,108. Health care and social work brought in roughly $3.9 billion in 2022, the biggest sector figure on the table, which tracks with the hospitals clustered in the city of Peoria.

Wikipedia lists an average January low of 14 degrees Fahrenheit and a July high of 86 for the county seat.

sections.h2: How does Peoria County bill property tax, and what does a late payment cost?
sections.html:
Each parcel gets a single annual bill that can be paid in two equal halves. The 2025 taxes, payable in 2026, came due June 9 and September 9, 2026, after bills were scheduled to go out by May 1. If nothing has arrived by May 15, call 672-6065 and choose option 5; the county says not receiving a bill is no excuse for skipping the payment.

There is no grace period on the county's page. Money that arrives or is postmarked after the due date picks up 1.5% for each month or part of one. Metered postage does not prove timeliness, and the Treasurer adds that the Peoria postal facility has stopped stamping postmarks, so mail early or use another channel.

  • Counter and mail payments can be cash (in the office only), personal check, cashier's check or money order.
  • Online and phone payments open after May 1. Cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal and Venmo carry a 2.65% convenience fee, and an electronic check costs $1.00.
  • Phone payments add $0.95 per parcel, and none of the processing fees go to the county.
  • A check returned by the bank costs $25.00.
  • A short payment is returned and the installment stays open, so cover the whole amount plus any penalty.

sections.h2: Which dates mattered on the 2025 Peoria County calendar?
sections.html:
These are the dates the county published for the 2025 tax year. They are behind us, yet the same order of events recurs each year with new days.

Peoria County calendar for 2025 taxes payable in 2026, from county Treasurer and Board of Review pages
StepDate posted by the county
Tax bills mailedBy May 1, 2026
First installmentJune 9, 2026
Second installmentSeptember 9, 2026
Board of Review filing deadlineSeptember 30, 2026
Final notices of unpaid tax mailedNo later than October 12, 2026
Last day to pay at the Treasurer to avoid the saleNovember 6, 2026, 5 p.m.
Annual tax saleNovember 9, 2026

The collector charges $10 once final notices are sent, covering registered mail and the published list, and the county page adds $113 at the sale itself. Have the Treasurer put the precise payoff in writing before money moves.

sections.h2: How does a Peoria County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1. The 2026 taxpayer notice sets the required level at 33.33% of fair market value, while the county's median level came in at 31.25%. An equalization factor is applied by township and class, exemptions come off, and the rate is multiplied against what remains.

The county strongly suggests an informal talk with the township assessor first. A formal Board of Review complaint can follow any time from June 1 up to 30 days after the newspaper prints your township's changes. The 2026 deadline on the Board's page was September 30, so that window is shut until June 1 of next year.

  • The form challenges value, not the size of the bill, and any change shows up on next year's bill rather than the one in hand.
  • Attach your evidence when you file. The Board can raise the value, lower it or confirm it.
  • A missed hearing is decided on the paperwork alone, and dates cannot be moved.
  • Packets are posted under Forms and Documents. Mail filings to Room 301 of the courthouse.

sections.h2: Which exemptions does Peoria County list?
sections.html:
Nearly all of these cut the equalized assessed value, so the dollar effect depends on your district's rate. The county's Tax Relief page describes them.

  • Owner-occupied (homestead): $6,000 off equalized assessed value for residents as of January 1. The township assessor initiates it, with no annual application.
  • Senior homestead: another $5,000 once you turn 65 in the tax year. File at the Assessor's Office with a deed copy and proof of age, one time only.
  • Senior assessment freeze: locks the taxable value for seniors under an income ceiling, with a new application each year. The page prints $65,000, so confirm with the Supervisor of Assessments what ceiling governs the year you file.
  • Returning veterans: a one-time $5,000 reduction.
  • Disabled persons: $2,000 reduction, renewed each year.
  • Disabled veterans: $2,500 for a 30% to under 50% service-connected rating, $5,000 for 50% to under 70%, and a fully exempt residence at 70% or higher.
  • Senior tax deferral: a 3% interest loan against the home, repaid at sale or death, with a March 1 filing deadline.

sections.h2: What happens to Peoria County taxes that stay unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent tax goes to a sale in early November. Registered buyers bid between 0% and 9% and the lowest number takes the lien. A parcel with no bidder is taken by Peoria County, as trustee for the districts, at 9%. That interest is charged at the sale and again every six months.

You remain the owner while the redemption clock runs, since what gets sold is the tax debt. Two years is the default and a buyer may push it to three, with the FAQ setting two and a half years as the floor for residences of one to six units. A judge reviews the buyer's request for a deed once time runs out.

To redeem, go to the County Clerk at 324 Main Street, Room 101, with a single payment of cash, a cashier's check or a money order made out to the Peoria County Clerk. Personal, business, mortgage and title company checks bounce back, and installment plans do not exist. Call (309) 672-6060; an online redemption estimate shows when the next penalty lands.

sections.h2: What should a Peoria County seller do about tax owed at closing?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the Treasurer for the current year and one from the Clerk if any year was sold, and hand both to the title company. Sold taxes are cleared by redemption at the Clerk's office, and because the payoff grows every six months, the number you use needs a date near closing.

At propertytax.peoriacounty.gov you can look up a parcel, its bill history and a printable bill. If the house is in the city of Peoria, find out whether you pay the City of Peoria Township Collector, because the county sets that office apart from its own counter. When a lender escrows the tax, confirm that the latest installment was credited to the right parcel number.

faqs.q: Where can Peoria County tax be paid at a counter?
faqs.a: At the Treasurer's office, 324 Main Street, Room G15, at a participating bank, or at a township collector. A bank needs the bill stub with the payment and takes it only until the second due date. The City of Peoria Township Collector serves its own residents.

faqs.q: What is the filing cutoff for a Peoria County complaint?
faqs.a: It closes 30 days after the newspaper publishes your township's changes, and it opens June 1. The Board listed September 30 for 2026, which has gone by. The Board of Review at 309-672-6022 can give next cycle's schedule.

faqs.q: Can I pay only part of an installment in Peoria County?
faqs.a: No. A partial payment is mailed back and the installment remains unpaid until the full amount, penalty included, comes in. Electronic payments that do not match the exact figure are rejected.

faqs.q: Does an owner-occupied exemption need a yearly application in Peoria County?
faqs.a: No. The township assessor sets up the $6,000 owner-occupied exemption without a yearly form. Seniors file the homestead exemption once, but the assessment freeze and the disabled persons exemption need renewing each year.

faqs.q: What is the redemption period after a Peoria County tax sale?
faqs.a: Two years is the default and the buyer can extend to three. For one-to-six unit homes the county FAQ sets a floor of two and a half years. Pay the County Clerk once, in full, with cash, a cashier's check or a money order.
